description: Drop unlinked income, group the rest by linked member, then compute shares, the average share, and summarise the above-average groups.

b.request: Among all income rows with a non-null `link_to_member`, sum `amount` per `link_to_member`, compute each member's total divided by the grand total of those member totals, and return one row (SUM of member totals for members whose share > average share, AVG of their shares, AVG of (share − average share) for those members) using unrounded values
b.sql: WITH member_totals AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(amount) AS total FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_member), shares AS (SELECT link_to_member, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM member_totals), stats AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), above AS (SELECT s.total, s.share, s.share - st.avg_share AS diff FROM shares s CROSS JOIN stats st WHERE s.share > st.avg_share) SELECT SUM(total) AS sum_member_totals_above_avg, AVG(share) AS avg_share_above_avg, AVG(diff) AS avg_diff_above_avg FROM above;

a.request: Group the income records by linked member (`income.link_to_member`), after first dropping every income record whose `link_to_member` is missing, so such income plays no part in anything below. Sum `amount` in each group. Each group's share is its sum divided by the sum of all the group sums; then take the plain average of the shares across groups. Keep only groups whose share is strictly greater than that average, and return one row with: (1) the total of their summed amounts, (2) the average of their shares, and (3) the average of (share minus average share). Do not round.
a.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(amount) AS s FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_member), sh AS (SELECT link_to_member, s, s * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(s) FROM g) AS share FROM g), avg_sh AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM sh), kept AS (SELECT sh.* FROM sh, avg_sh WHERE sh.share > avg_sh.a) SELECT SUM(s) AS total_amount, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - (SELECT a FROM avg_sh)) AS avg_share_deviation FROM kept;

c.request: Total up income `amount` by member (`link_to_member`) and work out each total's share of the sum of all the totals. For those whose share is strictly above the average share, give one row with: their combined amount, their average share, and the average amount by which their share is above the average share. No rounding. Drop unlinked income, group the rest by linked member, then compute shares, the average share, and summarise the above-average groups.
c.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(amount) AS total FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_member), shares AS (SELECT link_to_member, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM totals), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), above AS (SELECT s.total, s.share, a.avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT SUM(total) AS combined_amount, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS average_above_by FROM above;

d.request: Total up income `amount` by member (`link_to_member`), dropping any income with no linked member. For each linked member, work out their share of the sum of all the member totals. Then, for the members whose share is strictly above the average share, give one row with their combined amount, their average share, and the average amount by which their share is above the average share. No rounding.
d.sql: WITH member_totals AS (SELECT link_to_member AS member_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM income WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_member), shares AS (SELECT member_id, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM member_totals), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.total) AS combined_amount, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS average_share_above_avg FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;
